title: Test case: PICALM (ANTH) orchestration and productive-pit verdict
question: PICALM recruited to the membrane — can it support productive pit formation?

protein.name: PICALM
protein.role: size/regularity setter (Kaksonen); amphipathic ANTH wedge gives dome-level autonomous curvature

method: Ran PICALM's family-screen autonomous curvature as the wedge c_eff through the validated forward model (ccs_curvature), across an assembly ladder; read the dome/Omega stage vs the Omega/scission boundary. No force point-estimate — a stage/threshold call from the forward model.
verdict: NO — PICALM cannot support a productive pit on its own (autonomous P(cross Omega)=0.005; alone/coat/coat+actin all stay flat-to-dome, sub-threshold). The pit becomes productive (reaches Omega) only in the FULL assembly: clathrin coat + actin force + a crowding/curvature partner (epsin C-terminal IDP brush). This matches the established division of labour: PICALM sets vesicle size, epsin/crowding drives curvature.
caveat: Forward-model stage call using published/derived c_eff magnitudes, not an inverse on a measured curvature trajectory. The crowding partner contribution (epsin IDP brush c~0.025) is a representative co-player magnitude, not a measurement of this specific assembly.
